fieldValues.title: Container pointer writes refused when unresolved
fieldValues.decision_question: Must a container write (create or update) that points anchorInstanceId or identityInstanceId at an instance that is not a member be refused, or may it pass and leave the error for validation?
fieldValues.context: The exercise 'RFC-043 pointers' (3956749c, checked 2026-11-09 with release build.639) found that `container update {anchorInstanceId: <non-member>}`, `container create` with a non-member anchor, and `container update <root> {identityInstanceId: <non-member>}` each return ok, and `repo validate` then reports container-pointer-unresolved errors, while removing the member a pointer names is already refused ([R7], arrangement-pointer). RFC-043 [R3] says the pointer MUST equal a member, but [R7] mandates whole rejection only for [R2] violations and pointer-target removal. The analyst recommended 'A, after the client search shows no pointer-first writes'. That search was run on 2026-11-10: srs-web origin/main a0c7133 (essay-document.ts newEssay, site-edit.ts) and the muDemocracy site editor at b424f5e8 (site-editor/src/model.ts) set the pointers only in a create_container call whose memberInstanceIds already contains the same instance; no updateContainer call in either sets a pointer; srs-vscode (mutationCommands.ts) adds the member first and sets anchorInstanceId afterwards, deliberately, 'the earliest point a valid anchor exists'. No pointer-first write was found. The [R7] extension is an RFC-043 revision (Door 3) that cites this decision. Decision 0b1c25b1 requires a recorded ruling before the Third-party-ready group files a CLI, payload or WASM contract change; this record is that ruling.
fieldValues.friction: A write tool reports success for a change that leaves the repository invalid, and the error surfaces later, in validation, away from the write that caused it (SP-06, destructive and partial writes succeed silently).
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: 1. Refuse any write that leaves a pointer unresolved (recommended, the exercise's option A): extend [R7] so create and update are checked like removal, judged on the state after the whole write, so a create that names the anchor and lists it as a member in the same call passes. Leads to: invalid pointers cannot be written, matching affirmed remedy 'Every write refuses loudly what it cannot carry'. 2. Keep [R3] a validate-time rule (option B): writes may pass through an invalid state, which only matters to an editor that sets the pointer before adding the member, and none was found. 3. Do nothing: the asymmetry between removal (refused) and pointer moves (accepted) stays.
fieldValues.key_requirements: The check must judge the result of the whole write, never the order of fields within it, so the single-call create used by srs-web and the site editor stays valid. Create and update are treated alike. The refusal needs a stable error code so clients can branch on it. Trade-off: an editor that wants a two-step pointer-first flow must instead add the member first, as srs-vscode already does.
fieldValues.decision_statement: A container write that would leave anchorInstanceId or identityInstanceId naming a non-member is refused whole.
fieldValues.rationale: Removal of a pointed-at member is already refused, so refusing the symmetric case completes one rule rather than adding a new one. The client search found no editor that depends on passing through the invalid state, which was the only argument for option B.
fieldValues.revisit_when: A client needs to set a pointer before its member can exist (for example a multi-step import that cannot add members first); or a migration has to write containers whose pointers are repaired in a later step.
fieldValues.next_steps: After ratification: an RFC-043 revision extending [R7], and the srs-rust write-time check, filed as linked issues.
